text:
anya: heads up — found a redaction/order bug in the python sample app. when REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL=debug the underlying transport logs full headers before our redact hook runs, so Authorization appears in stdout. repro on sdk-python 0.9.2.

chris: can repro. simplest run: `REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL=debug python sample_app/main.py` where main calls client.completions.create(...). you'll see logs like `DEBUG:urllib3.connectionpool:Sending headers: {'Authorization': 'Bearer ...'}`. looks like middleware ordering in transport.

sam: temporary mitigation: set REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL=info in CI and dev machines. you can also set REDWOOD_REDACT_HEADERS=authorization,cookie as a config, but that only helps if the redactor runs before the logger.

leo: i'll open a tiny python sdk PR to ensure our redact middleware is registered before the http logging layer. also noticed an otel issue in JS sample: when otel sampling < 1.0 some requests don't get x-request-id injected by our otel hook. probable separate ordering bug in the trace/span creation path.

anya: for nextjs sample app I saw another quirk — the runtime/next fetch wrapper isn't forwarding traceparent into outbound requests if we call fetch('/api/llm') then forward that request to redwood sdk. using globalThis.fetch works. likely instrumentation patch misses next's fetch.

chris: agreed. add an e2e that runs Next dev server with instrumented fetch and asserts presence of `traceparent` and `x-request-id` on the outgoing call to Redwood. we should also assert that setting REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL=debug does NOT leak Authorization or cookie values.

leo: plan: python PR (redact-before-log), JS e2e for next fetch/traceparent, add unit to ensure x-request-id exists even when sampling drops spans. i'll tag them with devex/telemetry.

sam: QA checklist for fixes: 1) debug logs never print authorization or cookie values; 2) every outgoing request gets x-request-id header (even if span not sampled); 3) traceparent is forwarded when using Next runtime fetch; 4) sample-app README updated with REDWOOD_REDACT_HEADERS usage and how to run telemetry e2e.

anya: can someone add a short onboarding note in our quickstart about debug logging risk and how to avoid leaking tokens in local dev? new hires often run with REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL=debug by default.

chris: adding small blurb to quickstart and sample-app readme. also will instrument CI telemetry job to run with REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL=debug in a sandboxed env to make sure nothing leaks.

devex-bot: flaky label added to job telemetry-integration (https://ci.internal/telemetry/4821).

leo: PRs now: python SDK #2145 (redaction middleware order), sample-apps e2e #89 (next fetch instrumentation), js-sdk #912 (x-request-id injection fix). linking in the PR descriptions.

sam: drafting release note: "Fix: prevent debug logs from printing sensitive headers; ensure request ID propagation across runtimes; next.js fetch instrumentation restored." will circulate for approvals.

anya: thanks all. assigning followups: leo (python PR), chris (next e2e + quickstart blurb), sam (README + release note). paste any problematic logs here if you want me to scrub and attach to the PR. :thumbsup:
